abstract.para: By default, the &crmshell; obscures passwords in the output of commands like crm configure show. To further obscure sensitive values in the raw CIB data, you can use the crm resource secret command. This command replaces a resource parameter's value with a special string that points to a separate file containing the actual value. The file is not encrypted, but only the &rootuser; user has permission to read or modify it. This helps to prevent accidental data exposure.

step.para: Log in either as the &rootuser; user or as a user with sudo privileges.
Hide the value of a sensitive parameter:

listitem.para: To hide the value of an existing parameter, use the stash command:
listitem.screen: &prompt.user;sudo crm resource secret RESOURCE stash PARAMETER
&prompt.user;sudo crm resource secret mydb stash passwd

listitem.para: To add a new parameter, use the set command:
listitem.screen: &prompt.user;sudo crm resource secret RESOURCE set PARAMETER VALUE
&prompt.user;sudo crm resource secret mydb set passwd linux

step.para: Both of these commands move the value of the sensitive parameter to a separate file under the /var/lib/ directory. The file is not encrypted, but only the &rootuser; user has permission to read or modify it.
The cluster automatically synchronizes the change across the other nodes. However, if any nodes are unavailable, you might see the following output:
step.screen: Node bob is down - you'll need to update it with `cibsecret sync` later
step.para: When the node is available again, or if you add a new node to the cluster, you must manually synchronize the change:
You can view the hidden value with the following command:
step.screen: &prompt.user;sudo crm resource secret RESOURCE show PARAMETER
&prompt.user;sudo crm resource secret mydb show passwd

tip.para: crm resource secret is the crm front end for &pace;'s cibsecret command.
